**A model can help find suspicious labels, but disagreement does not prove the label is wrong.** Use out-of-fold probabilities so the model judging an example did not train on that example. High loss, disagreement, or confident-learning estimates can prioritize review. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00068)

A rare legitimate case can also have high loss because the model has not learned it. Automatically relabeling every difficult example would teach the dataset to agree with the model's current biases.

**Review a stratified sample.** Include likely errors, ordinary examples, rare classes, and important subgroups. Clarify annotation rules, adjudicate disagreements, and retain original labels and correction provenance. Measure the actual noise rate rather than accepting the proposed 15% as established fact.

Compare cleaned data and architecture changes separately on a fixed, clean evaluation set. Keep test labels out of tuning. Cleaning may reduce an inflated offline score by removing leakage or correcting a biased benchmark while improving validity. The useful outcome is better trustworthy performance, not merely a higher number on labels selected to flatter the current model.

**Technical details and references.**

Generate out-of-fold probabilities so suspicious labels are not judged by a model trained to memorize them. Confident learning estimates label-noise structure; high loss or disagreement helps prioritize examples for human review. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00068)

Do not automatically flip every high-loss label: rare valid cases, subgroup shift, and model bias also look difficult. Audit a stratified sample, document annotation rules, adjudicate disagreements, and preserve provenance. Correct train labels without using test labels to tune the model.

Compare old/new data and old/new architectures on a fixed clean evaluation set, reporting slice changes and uncertainty. The claimed 15% noise rate needs measurement. Cleaning may lower an inflated offline score while improving actual validity, so interpret gains in context.
